author: LegalEagle
description:
Attorney General Todd Blanche told Trump’s team he’s their lawyer, but that’s not how the Justice Department works 💼

Since the election, Blanche has been assuring administration officials that the DOJ has their backs: “If you work in this administration, you have a lawyer. It’s me, and we will defend you.” He has also said the department would defend Stephen Miller if Representative Robert Garcia’s oversight efforts target him.

But it’s called the Department of Justice for a reason, because justice itself is supposed to be the client. The DOJ does sometimes represent government officials and employees who are sued or subpoenaed, but in those cases, the client is the United States, not the individual employee.

The Constitution doesn’t mention the attorney general or the Justice Department at all. The office of attorney general wasn’t created until 1789, and the DOJ didn’t exist until 1870.

title: Todd Blanche Forgot Who the Justice Department Actually Works For
